samples.summary: `PresenceIdentityRepair` writes presence with `doc.update()` on every collaborative mount, including share-link viewers — bypassing every read-only presence gate this PR adds
samples.evidence: This PR's central premise is that any `doc.update()` on a viewer mount (presence included) is carried by the next `PushPull` with verb `rw`, which the now-enforcing-by-default webhook refuses, wedging the viewer's own sync. Every presence publisher was gated for that reason: `YorkieStore.updateSelection`/constructor (yorkie-store.ts:651, :102), `YorkieDocStore.updateCursorPos`/`publishResolvedLocalCursor` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1263, :3199), `readOnlyNoteStore`'s `setLocalSelection`, `slides-view.tsx:1150`, `board-view.tsx:601`, `pdf-collab.tsx:135`. `PresenceIdentityRepair` is mounted by `CollabDocumentProvider` (collab-document-provider.tsx:127) inside EVERY shared route — doc, note, board, slides, sheet, pdf — and at line 100 performs `doc.update((_root, presence) => presence.set(patch))` whenever any `initialPresence` key is missing after attach. It has no `readOnly`/role input at all, so nothing can hold it back on a viewer mount. It is deliberately an "opportunistic repair" for presence that did not land (i.e. it fires in exactly the cases the attach's presence was lost), and the notes route seeds `selection: null, cursor: null` (shared-document.tsx:998-999) — keys whose presence-after-attach is not something this code can assume. When it does fire on a viewer, it is the refused `rw` push the rest of the PR exists to prevent.

samples.summary: The writable half of the theme/master repair can persist `undefined` into `meta.themeId` / `meta.masterId` — the exact hazard the new read-path reconciliation was written to avoid
samples.evidence: `migrateDocument` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:110-121) deliberately reconciles only onto `firstStringId(...)`, documenting that assigning an id-less entry's `undefined` to a `string` field is worse than leaving the mismatch because `getActiveTheme` then matches `undefined === undefined` and renders from a palette-less theme. The CRDT-side repair it is paired with was not updated: `ensureSlidesRoot` still does `meta.themeId = rootAny.themes[0].id` (line 288) and `meta.masterId = rootAny.masters[0].id` (line 294) with no string check, so an editor mount of a deck whose first theme/master entry carries no `id` writes `undefined` into the document root — persisting the malformed state for every later reader, including the viewers the new read-path code is protecting. The two repairs now disagree about the same input.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as claimed: PresenceIdentityRepair (collab-document-provider.tsx:54-112) issues doc.update(...presence.set(patch)) at line 100 with no readOnly/role input, and is mounted unconditionally by CollabDocumentProvider (:127), which the share route uses for every document type and every role (shared-document.tsx:963,982,991,1006,1019, with initialPresence at :976,:985,:994-1000,:1009-1013,:1022). The PR's premise is genuine in this repo: the auth webhook denies PushPull with verb 'rw' for a share-link viewer while read-gating AttachDocument (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108,332-338,370), enforcement being the default (:120-142). Every other presence publisher is role-gated for that reason (yorkie-store.ts:81-113, :650-651; pdf-collab.tsx:135; yorkie-note-store.ts:415-421), leaving this repair as an ungated presence write reachable on viewer mounts in exactly the re-attach case the component exists to fix (:10-32). I found no guard or call-site condition making it unreachable for viewers, so the finding stands as a real, in-lane correctness gap.
